diagnostic_evidence.quote:
The potential function $V$  goes to infinity  near the obstacle and decays to zero at some positive level set far away from the obstacle $S$.
This ensures that  such an optimal trajectory does not intersect $S$.

issues.failure_explanation: Because the curve space already requires every φ(·,t) to be volume-preserving, δφ is constrained to the tangent space of Diff_vol and is not an arbitrary vector-valued variation. The pointwise Euler–Lagrange equation obtained by applying the fundamental lemma to arbitrary δφ therefore does not follow. More fundamentally, for every such φ, change of variables gives ∫_Ω V(φ(X,t))dX=∫_Ω V(x)dx, so the potential term is constant on the admissible configuration space. It cannot generate the asserted obstacle-avoidance force. Since φ is also onto Ω, a configuration of the whole fluid cannot avoid a nonempty spatial subset S⊂Ω.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must reformulate the admissible configuration space or the cost so that the obstacle term is not invariant under volume-preserving rearrangement, and then redo the constrained variational calculation with admissible variations.
issues.overall_effect: The stated adjoint necessary condition, the derivation of the modified Euler equation from it, and the advertised interpretation of V as altering the velocity to avoid an obstacle are unsupported. In the displayed modified equation, V is in any event absorbed by replacing p with p−V.
issues.title: The proof uses inadmissible variations and overlooks invariance of the potential
issues.why_classification: Preserving a genuine obstacle-avoidance effect requires changing the variational architecture, not a local proof correction; otherwise the central potential term has no effect on the fluid velocity.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\mathcal{J}(\varphi, v, \pi, k) = \int_{0}^{T} & \left[ \Big\langle \pi, v\circ \varphi - \frac{\partial \varphi}{\partial t} \Big\rangle - \frac{1}{2} \langle v,v \rangle \right. \\
        & \left. + \langle k\, \text{div}\, v + V\circ \varphi \rangle \right]

issues.failure_explanation: For the functional as displayed, the δφ coefficient is (Tv∘φ)^Tπ+∂tπ+grad V∘φ, so setting it to zero gives ∂tπ=−(Tv∘φ)^Tπ−grad V∘φ, not the stated plus sign. Conversely, because the constraint terms and kinetic term are written with the negative of the original objective, incorporating the original objective requires −V∘φ in J; that local sign change would yield the stated adjoint sign.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace +V∘φ by −V∘φ in the extended functional and carry that sign consistently through the variation and Theorem th2.
issues.overall_effect: As written, Theorem th1 is not the stationarity system of J, and the sign of the V term propagated into the modified Euler equation is not justified by that functional.
issues.title: The potential has the wrong sign in the extended functional
issues.why_classification: Independent of the deeper admissible-variation defect, this is a local sign repair that preserves the intended equations and does not require a new argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
To avoid collision with obstacles we introduce a potential function $V$ defined as the inverse value of the function $f$. The function $V$  goes to infinity  near the obstacle and decays to zero at some positive level set far away from the obstacle $S$.
This ensures that  such an optimal trajectory does not intersect $S$.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed V is undefined and singular on the sphere S, contradicting the stated smoothness on Ω. It is also negative on the sphere's interior and tends to −∞ when S is approached from inside, so minimization does not make it a globally repulsive barrier. Moreover, because each φ is a diffeomorphism onto Ω, V∘φ encounters the singular set whenever S⊂Ω, making the spatial cost integral ill-defined rather than proving avoidance.

failure_location.quote:
The potential function $V$ is an artificial smooth (or at least $C^{2}$) potential function
associated with a fictitious force inducing a repulsion from a region $S\subset\Omega$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must define a mathematically admissible obstacle-excluded domain or hard state constraint, or provide a well-defined barrier functional and prove existence, finiteness, and nonintersection for its extremals.
issues.overall_effect: The proposed example does not satisfy the regularity used in the variational calculations, and the asserted guarantee that the potential prevents intersection with S is not established.
issues.title: The proposed barrier is neither smooth on the fluid domain nor a valid two-sided repulsive potential
issues.why_classification: A smooth local replacement loses the claimed strict avoidance guarantee, while retaining a singular barrier requires a new domain and variational analysis.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The result of discretizing the first equation in \eqref{mod:eulereq} using a finite difference scheme may result in a discrete vector field with discrete divergence, even though we depart from divergence-free initial conditions.
$$\nabla^{d} \cdot X (i,j) = \frac{u(i+1,j) - u(i-1,j) + v(i, j+1) - v(i, j-1)}{2 \Delta x}.$$

issues.failure_explanation: Continuously, ∂xu+∂yv=sin x sin y+cos x cos y=cos(x−y), which is not zero. On the stated uniform periodic grid, the centered discrete divergence equals (sin(Δx)/Δx)cos(x_i−y_j), also nonzero in general. Thus the computation does not start from the divergence-free initial data claimed.

failure_location.quote: First, we used finite differences to approximate the solution of the first equation in \eqref{mod:eulereq} using as initial conditions the functions $u(x,y,0) = - \sin y \cos x$ and $v(x,y,0)= \sin y \cos x$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Project the initial field with the discrete Helmholtz projection before integration, or replace it by an explicitly divergence-free initial field and rerun the simulation.
issues.overall_effect: The reported experiment does not use admissible initial data for the incompressible system, so divergence observed later cannot be attributed only to discretization error.
issues.title: The stated initial velocity is not divergence-free
issues.why_classification: The defect has a routine local numerical repair, although the reported trajectory and figures would need recomputation.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The integration scheme uses an evenly spaced grid to integrate the vector field on the square $[0, 4\pi] \times [0, 4\pi]/\{0, 4\pi\}$ with discrete spacing between squares of $\Delta x = 4\pi/30$ and points lying in the border of the square identified.

issues.failure_explanation: On the stated 30-by-30 periodic grid, this stride-two Laplacian has checkerboard null modes in addition to constants. For example, φ(i,j)=(−1)^i has both zero centered discrete gradient and zero Δ^d. Hence the periodic Poisson problem does not determine φ uniquely, even after merely fixing its mean.

failure_location.quote: With suitable boundary conditions, this scalar field is unique.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State uniqueness only modulo the full checkerboard nullspace and impose one normalization per null mode, or use a compatible stencil without the extra decoupled parity modes.
issues.overall_effect: The specified Poisson solve is underdetermined unless additional nullspace conditions or a different discretization are supplied. The projected vector field can remain unique because the extra null modes have zero discrete gradient, but the claimed scalar-field uniqueness and an unqualified linear solve are invalid.
issues.title: The periodic centered Poisson operator is not uniquely invertible
issues.why_classification: This is a local discretization/nullspace correction and does not by itself change the projected velocity.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Using a small time step of $\Delta t = 1.5\times 10^{-3}$, we integrated the flow over $140$ steps.

issues.failure_explanation: The divergence-free condition is part of the evolution system and determines the pressure correction throughout time. Evolving an unconstrained field for 140 steps and projecting only the final result allows non-divergence-free components to enter the nonlinear advection term at every intermediate step. A final projection cannot undo that altered evolution.

failure_location.quote: Therefore, after the time integration stage is completed we projected our solution to a divergence free-vector field using the approach explained in the previous section.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a pressure/projection method that enforces the discrete divergence constraint at every time step, with a specified consistent update and boundary treatment, and rerun the computation.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed output is not established to approximate a solution of the incompressible modified Euler equations, even if its final discrete divergence is zero.
issues.title: A projection only after all time steps does not integrate the incompressible equation
issues.why_classification: Repair requires changing the time-stepping algorithm and recomputing the simulation, but it is a contained numerical-method modification rather than new global theory.
